title: Family and my, your, his, her (Meine Familie)
summary: Talk about your family, and say whose something is: mein, dein, Ihr, sein, ihr, unser.
goals: Say his, her, our: sein, ihr, unser
Say whether you are married and have brothers or sisters

nicosWeg.title: Nicos Weg A1, chapter 15: Family (for the family words)
Nicos Weg A1, chapter 6: Living (Unser Haus: possessives)

points: Parents: [[der Vater]], [[die Mutter]], together [[die Eltern]] (plural, so [[meine Eltern]]).
Siblings: [[der Bruder]], [[die Schwester]], together [[die Geschwister]] (brothers and sisters).
Grandparents: [[der Großvater]] or [[Opa]], [[die Großmutter]] or [[Oma]], together [[die Großeltern]].
More family: [[der Onkel]], [[die Tante]], [[der Cousin]] (male cousin), [[die Cousine]] (female cousin).
[[mein]] goes with der and das words, [[meine]] with die words and plurals: [[mein Vater]], [[meine Mutter]], [[meine Eltern]].
[[Meine Familie ist groß.]] or [[Meine Familie ist klein.]] To ask: [[Wie groß ist deine Familie?]]

phrases.en: These are my brothers and sisters.

phrases.de: Das ist mein Großvater. Er ist mein Opa.
phrases.en: This is my grandfather. He's my grandpa.

points: Each personal pronoun has its possessive: [[ich]] [[mein]], [[du]] [[dein]], [[er]] and [[es]] [[sein]], [[sie]] (she) [[ihr]], [[wir]] [[unser]], [[ihr]] (you all) [[euer]], [[sie]] (they) [[ihr]], [[Sie]] [[Ihr]].
Two steps: first pick by the owner (my, your, his ...), then the ending by the thing owned.
With der and das nouns there is no ending: [[mein Fernseher]], [[mein Auto]]. With die nouns and plurals, add -e: [[meine Katze]], [[meine Bücher]].
[[euer]] drops an e when it gets the ending: [[euer Auto]], but [[eure Katze]].
Polite [[Ihr]] has a capital I, whether you speak to one person or several. [[ihr]] for 'her' and 'their' is small.

phrases.de: Das ist Peter. Das ist sein Auto.
phrases.en: This is Peter. This is his car.

phrases.de: Das ist Lena. Das ist ihr Auto.
phrases.en: This is Lena. This is her car.

phrases.de: Herr Müller, ist das Ihr Auto?
phrases.en: Mr Müller, is this your car?

phrases.de: Sie wohnen in Deutschland. Das ist ihr Haus.
phrases.en: They live in Germany. This is their house.

points: [[Ihr]] with a capital I is the polite 'your', for [[Sie]]: [[Wie ist Ihr Familienname?]]
Small [[ihr]] has four jobs. First, 'you' for two or more people you say du to: [[Kinder, habt ihr Hunger?]]
Second and third, 'her' and 'their': [[Das ist Eva. Das ist ihr Haus.]], [[Das sind meine Eltern. Das ist ihr Haus.]]
Fourth, 'to her', the dative of [[sie]] (she): [[Ich gebe ihr eine Blume.]] The dative comes in Unit 6.
In a letter or message to someone you know, you may capitalise the informal 'you': [[Habt Ihr am Wochenende Zeit?]] It's optional.

phrases.de: Herr Müller, ist das Ihr Auto?
phrases.en: Mr Müller, is that your car?

phrases.de: Max und Lena, habt ihr am Wochenende Zeit?
phrases.en: Max and Lena, are you free at the weekend?

phrases.de: Das ist meine Schwester. Das ist ihr Buch.
phrases.en: This is my sister. This is her book.

phrases.de: Das sind unsere Nachbarn. Das ist ihr Sohn.
phrases.en: These are our neighbours. This is their son.

phrases.de: Meine Oma wohnt in Berlin. Ich fahre heute zu ihr.
phrases.en: My grandma lives in Berlin. I'm going to see her today.

notes.extra: [[ihr]] as 'to her' (dative), which the lesson leaves for Unit 6.

sections.title: mein and meine
sections.text:
[[mein]] (my) works like [[ein]]: [[mein Bruder]], [[mein Kind]], but **meine** with feminine nouns and with every plural: [[meine Schwester]], [[meine Eltern]].

The same goes for [[dein]] (your, informal) and [[Ihr]] (your, polite): [[dein Bruder]], [[deine Schwester]], [[Ihre Familie]].

[[euer]] (your, to several friends) drops an e when it gets the ending: [[euer Sohn]], but [[eure Eltern]].

sections.title: my, your, his, her, our, their

sections.text: [[sein]] also means 'his' (not only 'to be'), and [[ihr]] also means 'her' and 'their'. The context tells you which: [[Das ist sein Bruder.]] = That is his brother. [[Ihr Name ist Anna.]] = Her name is Anna. At the start of a sentence, Ihr can also be the polite 'your'; the context decides.

German has no Russian свой: 'Hayk loves his sister' (Айк любит свою сестру) is simply [[Hayk liebt seine Schwester.]]

Armenian often uses a suffix (եղբայրս = my brother). German always puts a separate word in front: [[mein Bruder]].

items.de: Hast du Geschwister? - Ja, ich habe einen Bruder und eine Schwester.
items.en: Do you have brothers or sisters? - Yes, I have a brother and a sister.
items.note: einen Bruder: see lesson 6 of this unit.
das + sind for more than one person or thing

items.de: Bist du verheiratet? - Nein, ich bin ledig.
items.en: Are you married? - No, I'm single.

items.de: Das ist meine Schwester. Ihr Name ist Anna.
items.en: This is my sister. Her name is Anna.

items.de: Wie viele Geschwister hast du? - Zwei.
items.en: How many brothers and sisters do you have? - Two.

sections.text: Family is normal small talk with friends and classmates. With colleagues you have just met, Germans usually stick to work, hobbies and weekend plans at first.

items.question: Which sentence means 'Her name is Anna'?
items.explanation: ihr = her; sein = his; mein = my.
Eltern is plural, so meine, and the verb is wohnen.
